title: Rukmini Kalyanam
body:
Rukmini Kalyanam

Rukmini, princess of Vidarbha, was the very embodiment of beauty, virtue, and devotion. Though she had never seen Krishna, her heart belonged to Him, for from childhood she had heard of His divine pastimes — the slaying of Kansa, the lifting of Govardhan, His boundless compassion for His devotees. From the words of sages, travelers, and poets she had gathered a picture of a Lord whose every action was rooted in dharma and love, and the more she heard, the deeper her love grew, until she resolved to accept no one but Shri Krishna as her husband.
But fate seemed to work against her. Her elder brother Rukmi was a staunch adversary of Krishna, and disregarding his sister's wishes he arranged her marriage to his close friend Shishupala, king of Chedi and Krishna's sworn enemy, determined that she should never be united with Krishna. As the wedding preparations went forward Rukmini found herself trapped in despair, but she was not one to surrender. On the night before the wedding she summoned Sunanda, a trusted brahmana messenger, and entrusted him with a letter to be carried with all haste to Dwaraka and placed in Krishna's own hands.
In the letter she poured out her heart, telling Krishna that she had heard of His glories and His kindness toward those who take refuge in Him, that she had surrendered her heart and soul to Him alone, and that cruel fate now sought to bind her to a man she did not love. She wrote that on the morning of the wedding she would visit the temple of Goddess Parvati at dawn, and that she would await Him there; if He did not come, she would surrender her life, for a life without Him was a fate worse than death. She begged Him to come swiftly and claim her as His own, just as Lord Vishnu had rescued the Earth from the depths of the ocean.
Deeply moved by her devotion and urgency, Krishna wasted no time. Summoning His charioteer Daruka, He set out for Vidarbha with the speed of the wind. As dawn broke, Rukmini walked gracefully to the temple of Parvati, performed her prayers, and deliberately lingered, buying time for Krishna to arrive. Just as she stepped out of the temple, Krishna appeared like a streak of lightning; before anyone could react He lifted her into His chariot and rode away.
News of the abduction spread swiftly, and Rukmi, enraged and humiliated, set out with his army and several allied kings to pursue Krishna and reclaim his sister. Catching up, Rukmi ordered his forces to attack, and a fierce battle erupted, arrows raining down upon Krishna. But Krishna countered every assault with effortless grace, His bow Sharnga cutting through the enemy ranks, while Balarama joined the fray and scattered the army with sheer force, until Rukmi's forces lay in ruins. Rukmi himself then stood before Krishna, defiant yet outmatched; Krishna broke his bow with a single shot and struck aside his sword, leaving him defenseless. As Krishna raised His weapon to deliver the final blow, Rukmini rushed forward and fell at His feet, pleading that He spare her brother, for though he had wronged her, she could not bear to see his life taken. Honoring her request, Krishna spared Rukmi's life, but as a mark of humiliation cut off half of his moustache and hair, leaving him disgraced.
With Rukmi defeated, Krishna and Rukmini proceeded to Dwaraka, where their wedding was celebrated with unparalleled joy, the Devas themselves showering flowers from the heavens. Thus Rukmini became the chief queen of Dwaraka and the beloved of Shri Krishna, the very embodiment of devotion and surrender — proof that true love, joined with devotion and determination, always triumphs.
